diego: hey all :wave: diego here, just joined eng. Quick newbie Q: should I use a hosted API key or the sandbox key for local dev? Where do I find the sandbox key in the Console? Also curious about default sandbox limits and how to request a short spike increase for a demo.

neel: welcome! use the SANDBOX key for development and experiments — hosted keys are billable and for prod. Console path: Settings -> API Keys -> Sandbox (it's a separate section). Defaults are intentionally small: ~100 req/min, up to ~8 req/sec burst, and we enforce soft token/day caps (~500k tokens/day for new orgs). Streaming has separate concurrent-stream limits (typical sandbox = 6).

infra-bot: Automated tip: If your account didn't get a sandbox key, run: `curl -sS https://internal-api.redwood.ai/users/me/keys --header "Authorization: Bearer $SSO_TOKEN"` (SSO required) or open a ticket in #help with subject "missing sandbox key".

devex: Sandbox usage is covered by onboarding credits and won't charge your org card. You can still see sandbox traffic in Console -> Usage (labelled "Sandbox / Onboarding"). For temporary increases: use https://intranet.redwood.ai/onboarding -> select "sandbox bump" and include expected qps, duration, model, and contact. DevEx typically responds same day for short demo windows. You can also DM @neel if it's urgent.

neel: practical tip: implement client-side exponential backoff + jitter for 429s. For demos where you need short bursts, request a bump and reduce tokens per request (shorter context, smaller max_tokens) to stay under caps.

diego: super helpful, thanks everyone :rocket: I'll file the bump form and DM @neel with the demo plan.
